args: Analyze the root cause and best minimal fix for the xmlAddRef use-after-free in libxml2/valid.c. Specifically, what reliable signal distinguishes streaming xmlTextReader validation from persistent-tree validation at xmlAddRef call sites, and are there existing APIs/flags or attribute-removal hooks that keep doc->refs synchronized? Assess whether always storing a copied attribute name (ret->name) and setting ret->attr=NULL is semantically safe, including diagnostics and public API behavior.

The ASan crash occurs during xmlTextReader parsing with DTD validation: xmlAddRef in libxml2/valid.c stores ret->attr based only on ctxt->vstateNr != 0. A malformed/duplicate declaration leaves vstateNr == 0, so the reader later frees/recycles the attribute in xmlTextReaderFreeProp (libxml2/xmlreader.c), while doc->refs retains it. xmlValidateDocumentFinal then calls xmlValidateRef and dereferences freed attr->name. The current streaming branch copies attr->name and records line number, while the nonstreaming branch retains attr. Call sites include SAX2.c, xmlValidateOneAttribute in valid.c, namespace validation, and xmlschemastypes.c with ctxt NULL. We need a root-cause fix confined to C/C++ files under libxml2 and should preserve persistent DOM behavior where possible.
